primitiveReview.name: read_bounded_reserved_with_postchecks<R: Read, E: From<ReadFailure>>
primitiveReview.budgetPartition: read share carved with the accepted 41 with_allowance, so the read cannot consume postcheck space (the failure root demonstrated at 431)
primitiveReview.documentsTheTrap: doc states the parent must already hold read PLUS postcheck allowance, and that for WorkLedger::effect the total goes in the second argument because the first is charged but not spendable
primitiveReview.typeLevelProvisionality: inner closure returns Result<Result<Vec<u8>, ReadFailure>, WorkFailure<E>>: the outer arm carries terminal failures, the inner arm the provisional outcome
primitiveReview.noEarlyEscape: callback takes (&R, &mut ReservedPostchecks) and returns Result<(), _>, so it sees neither the accumulated Vec nor the pending outcome and has no channel to emit anything
primitiveReview.borrowing: read_charged(&mut reader, ..) borrows mutably only inside the with_allowance closure, so the later &reader borrow is conflict-free; works because &mut R: Read
primitiveReview.precedence: a postcheck error returns through ? and discards pending, outranking a pending read error - matching read_one's existing order
primitiveReview.finalization: only after callback success is a pending read error converted into E and returned as Operation, closing the owner; bytes require both read and callback success
primitiveReview.fileFixtureProvesOnly: ptr::from_ref equality plus dev/ino/len at callback time show the same object; the test comment says plainly this is usable borrow, not custody

limits: A sequencing primitive for an ARBITRARY callback: it orders read, checks and finalization but does not establish that any actual native check occurred, and no such inference is drawn.

Existing native adapters are not rewired; complete 429 native composition remains open. The owner still owes real descriptor, directory, name, account and custody checks and properly derived costs; ACL and descriptor costs remain unresolved.
Standalone read_bounded_accounted and read_bounded_reserved are unchanged and still latch ordinary I/O before returning; the header now names them explicitly.
EOF is relative to the Read contract; arbitrary reader, callback and drop internals, OS, service and allocator costs, RSS and latency are outside the claim.
No new authority, creator, P0 or current authority; no Linux, release, power-loss, full M2 or M2-M6 qualification; existing law unchanged.
Root substantive assent and guarded private/live integration remain required.
observations: The callback cannot return data. Result<(), _> is the safe choice - no channel to leak a provisional outcome - but a real postcheck producing an observation must capture it into a closure local. Ergonomic friction worth knowing before the native adapter is written.

InvalidLimit remains terminal and latching, now converted into the caller's E. My runtime40 note stands: a caller parameter error still closes the shared operation, and validating max before the bracket would keep a misuse from poisoning a healthy operation.

read_allowance is unvalidated against the parent's remainder by design - an over-large value refuses through with_allowance and is terminal, which is correct, but a sizing mistake presents as budget exhaustion rather than a distinguishable misuse. Acceptable while costs are underived; it matters more once real postcheck costs exist.
